Build protocol

Three builds per implementation on the same Azure worker, with alternating order and generated outputs cleared. Installed dependencies are reused; installation is timed separately and excluded from the build figures. The original command compiles its Git checkout using its native build tools. For packages authored in JavaScript, this can include generated declarations and type checks. Production ESM assembly is an additional, separately measured step.

The workers are Azure Standard_D16als_v7 machines, AMD EPYC 9V45, 16 vCPUs, 31.3 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 and Node 24.11.1. They belong to a shared pool; wall times include possible contention. Package output scopes differ, so these figures are not presented as build speedup ratios. The PostHog and PlayCanvas ports cover selected portions of their upstream repositories.

Monaco and Vue do not complete with the measured compiler. React Markdown has a dependency declaration failure after its runtime tests pass; Remark has a failing closed-entry check. Those limitations remain explicit. Passing recorded checks does not establish complete API parity for partial implementations.

Motion browser performance

Thirty paired trials per passing workload after two warmups per lane. Both sides use identical visible elements, CSS, keyframes, easing, duration and viewport. Every element is checked at five paused positions and at completion. Native animation calls, options and active properties must match before timing; additional natural-playback checks inspect every animated property on every element to verify continuous progress. The exact 312-export ESM graphs, using the same minifier versions and public extern reservations, are used for both size and performance; the native 52-export default port entry is recorded separately.

Behavior contract. Native eligibility, string/color interpolation, easing, repeat timing, controls, interruption and library frame scheduling are compared with the source-built original. Apparent style/layout savings alone cannot establish matching behavior. The remaining CPU differences below apply to the checked workloads.

Current size. The matched 312-export Motionlil graph is 174,382 raw bytes and 51,351 Brotli bytes; original Motion is 134,557 raw and 39,902 Brotli bytes. The full port still misses the smaller-bundle goal. The default port entry is a narrower consumer API at 122,396 raw and 35,197 Brotli bytes, so its size is listed separately.

Matched mangling and scope

Both lanes use esbuild 0.28.1, Terser 5.51.2, ES2022 and three compression passes. Every property-mangled pair uses identical reservations. Public builds reserve public API, browser and dynamic names. Closed builds transform the same caller with the library and reserve browser/dynamic protocols; other properties can be renamed. The full closed diagnostic also retains all 312 roots under identical short export aliases. Closed sizes include the caller and are not public ESM distributions.

Each 312-export public mode passes 39 browser checks against the original with unchanged property names. All 72 closed comparisons match their checked values, native timing and RAF behavior. The public mix overload now supports the original two-argument mixer and three-argument numeric forms. These tests cover selected scenarios; low-level layout/rendering adapters remain incomplete. The gap persists under identical mangling policies. Earlier measurements used different esbuild/Terser versions and different property rules; this corrected comparison still shows real port overhead. The other 26 library cards retain their recorded measurements and pins.

The headline bundle/minify assembly took 0.650 s for Motion and 1.096 s for LilScript on the recorded worker (one assembly sample each). These are separate from the three clean native package-build timings.

Compiler and implementation findings

Ordinary LilScript type annotations are compile-time information and do not add runtime validation. Explicit source type tests and conversions retain runtime semantics. The port still contains more explicit dynamic guards and JavaScript boundary adapters than original Motion; static typing has removed redundant guards from control options, callbacks, numeric state and value types. Remaining size and CPU differences are not explained solely by the DOM/CSSOM bottleneck.

The current package compiles one shared graph. Feature imports share constructors, caches and frame queues; native controls use shared prototype methods. Checked pure factories support removal of unused initialization. Completion promises, caller-owned keyframe arrays, option getters and null/undefined handling follow the checked original contracts.

Compiler regressions preserve native-class helpers and callback variables captured inside template expressions. Higher JavaScript optimization settings are evaluated separately from the measured production configuration, which uses level 0 plus the same recorded Terser pipeline. The compiler has 1,635 passing library tests locally. These checks do not establish complete API parity: low-level layout/rendering adapters remain incomplete.

Headless renderer CPU does not include all GPU/compositor work. Full table, methodology and raw samples.
